entries.root_cause: Tenant-scoped trace identifiers were unequal across tenants but were produced by a public deterministic SHA-256 transform, so an observer with one exported identifier and the target tenant identifier could derive the other tenant representation and join protected telemetry.
horizontal_audit: cross-tenant rescoping from an authenticated prior export
behavior when no secret tenant-scope authority is available

entries.root_cause: The learning resolver proved reachability of falsifier calls inside main but did not prove that the module execution path actually invokes main, allowing the complete falsification suite to become dead code while still receiving executable guardrail credit.
horizontal_audit: reachability inside main after entrypoint reachability

entries.root_cause: Issue-comment reconciliation resolved and checked out the pull-request head but the GitHub Actions run itself remained associated with the default-branch SHA, so a failed late reconciliation could leave the earlier green PR-head check untouched.
horizontal_audit: stable status context on the reviewed head

entries.root_cause: A falsifier could remain reachable and named from main while its body was replaced by pass or return, so call-graph reachability alone still allowed a credited guardrail that performed no negative assertion or mutation check.

Material-finding detection depended on the Codex renderer-specific phrase P1 Badge, so conventional priority-prefixed review text such as [P1] could bypass ledger reconciliation despite being semantically merge-blocking feedback.
